PR #42 is merged - make a follow-up:

Given the tracker coverage to |eta|<4 and the luminous region the outer pixel discs can drop some of the inner rings, optimize that.
I’ll inspect the merged disc design, derive the required inner radius at each disc from |η| < 4 and the luminous region, and open a follow-up PR with the optimized layout and validation.

For removing inner rings, should I preserve all charged tracks on their first outward traversal, or use a minimum transverse momentum? The first option needs no new momentum threshold and will be more conservative.
- Preserve all pT on first outward traversal
- Use pT ≥ 1 GeV
- Use straight-ray geometry only

PR42 was merged into the prototype branch rather than main, so I’ll use that exact merge as the baseline. The straight-ray bound is \(r_\min=(|z|-150\,\mathrm{mm})/\sinh(4)\); I’m also checking magnetic bending before deciding which whole rings can be removed safely.

I’ll use pT ≥ 1 GeV, including both charge signs and the existing 2–4 T field hypotheses. The ACTS preflight still reports changed environment fingerprints, so I’ll verify the installed runtime before running the native checks.

The study removes ring 1 from discs 5–6, rings 1–2 from disc 7, and rings 1–3 from discs 8–9, on both ends and for both layouts. That saves 424 chips and about 1.14 kW of nominal heat.

The fourth ring on the last disc remains useful once transverse vertex offsets are included. The 1,906 matched analytic tracks preserve every baseline hit within the requested scope; I’m now checking the boundary cases with ACTS.

ACTS confirms that the trimming preserves all in-scope hit sets, including 1 GeV tracks of both charge signs in 4 T. It also confirms that the first retained ring on each disc is still reachable.

The mixed layout’s reference trunk demand drops from 1.089× to 1.032× capacity. That is an improvement, but cable packing still needs further work; the service radii remain unchanged.

The optimized schedule removes inner rings from discs 5–9 on both ends, saving 424 chips in either layout. Ring 4 stays on the last disc: ACTS confirms that 1 GeV tracks from the luminous-region boundary can reach it. I’m finishing the report, repository checks and follow-up PR.

Both layouts keep their module orientations, disc positions and service-radius limits. The trimming also removes 40 cooling circuits and saves about 1.14 kW of nominal chip power. Service demand falls, but the existing trunk and neck packing failures remain open.

The nine focused tests, seven inherited support checks and all 31 dashboard tests pass. The report now includes the before/after layouts and the removal schedule for every disc. I’m publishing the follow-up against the prototype branch where PR #42 was merged.

[PR #43](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/43) is open with the removal table, figures and reproducible validation. The final metadata update is pushed; I’m checking the hosted build. The session log is also synchronized to your original checkout, with exact token recovery pending until this turn closes.
The hosted build for the final revision has started; GitHub cancelled the earlier build when the metadata update arrived. Local validation is complete, and I’m waiting for this final CI result.

The report includes deliberate tracks beyond |η| = 4 that lose hits after trimming, alongside the in-scope tracks whose hits are preserved. Existing seam and edge gaps remain documented. CI is currently running the finite-module coverage controls.

CI has passed the finite-module controls and moved on to the barrel coverage checks. The PR documents the operating assumptions: pT ≥ 1 GeV, |η| ≤ 4, the bounded luminous region and a uniform axial field up to 4 T.

The hosted geometry and aperture test stages are complete. Dashboard, logging and documentation checks are running now. The PR leaves the support plate intact and removes the unused modules, pickups and cooling circuits.

Opened [PR #43](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/43), using **pT ≥ 1 GeV**. Both layouts use this schedule on both ends:

| Discs | Inner rings removed |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | None |
| 5–6 | Ring 1 |
| 7 | Rings 1–2 |
| 8–9 | Rings 1–3 |

This saves **424 chips, 1.14 kW nominal power and 40 cooling circuits**. Surviving orientations, positions and service-radius bounds stay fixed. Ring 4 remains necessary on the last disc.

Per layout, 1,906 analytic tracks and 182 in-scope native ACTS tracks preserve every baseline hit. Hosted CI passed. The result assumes the bounded luminous region and uniform axial fields up to 4 T; existing coverage gaps and service packing failures remain unresolved.
